title: Curiosity rover point-of-view images, Mount Sharp boxwork (sols 4500-5073)
generated_by: tools/pov_build.py (see its header for method and sources)

frame.app: X = easting - 8144000 (east), Y = elev_geoid + 3863 (up), Z = -(northing + 285200) (-Z is north); metres in the map projection (Mars 2000 sphere equirectangular, R 3396190 m, centre lon 0)
frame.pos: camera entrance pupil (CAHVOR C) for images; rover nav frame origin (ground under the turn-in-place axis) for stops
frame.look: unit vector through the image centre pixel (the boresight), app frame
frame.up: unit vector toward the top of the image at its centre, orthogonal to look
frame.corners: unit rays through the outer corners of the top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left pixels, app frame (lens distortion included)
frame.hfov_vfov: degrees between the rays through the left/right (top/bottom) image edges at the centre row (column), from the CAHVOR/CAHVORE model
frame.az_el: boresight azimuth (deg clockwise from north) and elevation (deg above the local level plane) in the site frame
frame.width_height: pixels of the saved file; model_width/height = pixels of the original product (the grid the camera model is defined on)

sources.mastcam_pointing: https://planetarydata.jpl.nasa.gov/img/data/msl/msl_mmm/ (PDS4 labels and RAW_INDEX tables, Release 42, to sol 4843)
sources.frames: PDS MSLNAV_0XXX/DOCUMENT/MSL_COORDINATE_FRAMES.PDF; MSL Camera & LIBS EDR/RDR SIS v4.1 (JPL D-38107); GEOMETRIC_CM.TXT (CAHV/CAHVOR/CAHVORE, Gennery)

notes: Mastcam frames after sol 4843 are not included: the raw-image API gives no pointing for Mastcam and PDS has released Mastcam labels only to sol 4843 (Release 42).

Navcam is stored at up to 768 px and Front Hazcam at up to 640 px (originals 1024 px), Mastcam at up to 1024 px, all JPEG quality 85, to fit about 60 MB; the url field links the full-resolution original.
Stops without a waypoint (mid-drive imaging) are placed from the nearest waypoint of the same site plus the site-frame telemetry displacement (position_source says which).

Navcam and Mastcam are near-perspective (CAHVOR): a frustum from pos/look/up/hfov/vfov, or the corner rays, matches the photo to a fraction of a pixel at the centre. Front Hazcam is a fish-eye (CAHVORE, 126 deg edge to edge, corner rays ~90 deg off axis): it does not fit a rectilinear frustum; show it as a flat picture placed along look/up.
Stops with an empty images list are mid-drive stops (Hazcam during drives) kept for position only, or stops whose frames lost out in the 60 MB budget to views from nearby stops.

The 7 EVA science stops (116_1944, 117_1122, 118_198, 118_1752, 119_846, 120_82, 120_2366) carry extra views from tools/pov_enrich.py: up to 10 more Navcam frames for 360 deg coverage (any Navcam eye and product type, native size up to 1024 px) and up to 6 Mastcam colour frames. Navcam subframe, mixed and downsampled products are partial or half-resolution frames; width/height give their size.

gain and sky (tools/pov_blend.py) are display aids for the photos hung in 3D: gain is a brightness multiplier that makes overlapping photos at one stop agree, sky lists per column strip (16, left to right) the fraction of image height from the top where the sky ends, so the app can fade the photo out above it. The image files are untouched.
